literal: People made another rhyme: "Qudi may be steep—what good are bandits? As long as Lord Song keeps them off himself."
idiomatic: People made another rhyme: "Qudi may be steep—what good are bandits? As long as Lord Song keeps them off himself."

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi there was a great amnesty; the commandery had not a single prisoner—the officials merely bowed to the edict.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi there was a great amnesty; the commandery had not a single prisoner—the officials merely bowed to the edict.

literal: Inside the prison even mice and peach trees were overgrown with wormwood.
idiomatic: Inside the prison even mice and peach trees were overgrown with wormwood.

literal: Daily the gate of the yamen stood empty and still, with no more litigants; people called it the Spirit Gate.
idiomatic: Daily the gate of the yamen stood empty and still, with no more litigants; people called it the Spirit Gate.

literal: That winter sweet springs appeared within the borders.
idiomatic: That winter sweet springs appeared within the borders.

literal: When his replacement arrived the whole city saw him off on the road.
idiomatic: When his replacement arrived the whole city saw him off on the road.

literal: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward to thank him: "This old man is ninety and remembers thirty-five administrations.
idiomatic: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward to thank him: "This old man is ninety and remembers thirty-five administrations.

literal: My lord was not only good in government—his clarity went to the bottom.
idiomatic: My lord was not only good in government—his clarity went to the bottom.

literal: Now that we lose such a man, how can the people be saved?"
idiomatic: Now that we lose such a man, how can the people be saved?"

literal: None failed to cling to his carriage and weep.
idiomatic: None failed to cling to his carriage and weep.

literal: Later he died as Governor of Dongjun and was posthumously made Governor of Xinzhou.
idiomatic: Later he died as Governor of Dongjun and was posthumously made Governor of Xinzhou.

literal: Shiliang studied hard, loved composing text, and wrote five chapters of "Summary of Characters" and ten rolls of "Song Clan Separate Records."
idiomatic: Shiliang studied hard, loved composing text, and wrote five chapters of "Summary of Characters" and ten rolls of "Song Clan Separate Records."

literal: His son Bozong held the post of Attending Censor.
idiomatic: His son Bozong held the post of Attending Censor.

literal: By nature retiring and fond of learning, he wrote much.
idiomatic: By nature retiring and fond of learning, he wrote much.

literal: When Qi fell he did not change office and therefore never entered service.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he did not change office and therefore never entered service.

literal: At the beginning of Daye in Sui he died at home.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye in Sui he died at home.

literal: Shiliang's younger brother Shigui.
idiomatic: Shiliang's younger brother Shigui.

literal: From youth Shigui disciplined himself and loved the law.
idiomatic: From youth Shigui disciplined himself and loved the law.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he successively held the three Secretariat posts, the offices of two-thousand-bushel rank, and Director of the Ministry of Justice, with concurrent Long History of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he successively held the three Secretariat posts, the offices of two-thousand-bushel rank, and Director of the Ministry of Justice, with concurrent Long History of Bingzhou.

literal: He held the prisons with leniency and fairness and saved many.
idiomatic: He held the prisons with leniency and fairness and saved many.

literal: As Director of the Ministry of Justice there was a prisoner wronged in his case who was about to be sent off and nearly executed.
idiomatic: As Director of the Ministry of Justice there was a prisoner wronged in his case who was about to be sent off and nearly executed.

literal: Shigui sent riders to pursue and stop it, memorialized urgently on the facts, and he was spared.
idiomatic: Shigui sent riders to pursue and stop it, memorialized urgently on the facts, and he was spared.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice-Director of the Court of Justice.
idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Vice-Director of the Court of Justice.

literal: People of Luozhou gathered planning to rob the He Bridge; officials arrested and tried them, implicating more than seventeen hundred Yuan partisans.
idiomatic: People of Luozhou gathered planning to rob the He Bridge; officials arrested and tried them, implicating more than seventeen hundred Yuan partisans.

literal: Cui Ang was Vice-Director of the Court and treated it as rebellion; for years it was not decided.
idiomatic: Cui Ang was Vice-Director of the Court and treated it as rebellion; for years it was not decided.

literal: When Shigui became Vice-Director he judged the affair as robbery, executed only the ringleaders, and released all the rest who followed.
idiomatic: When Shigui became Vice-Director he judged the affair as robbery, executed only the ringleaders, and released all the rest who followed.

literal: Chief Justice Su Zhenzhi was known for fair competence; within the office they said: "To decide doubtful cases, Su Zhenzhi; to see the inside from the outside, Song Shigui."
idiomatic: Chief Justice Su Zhenzhi was known for fair competence; within the office they said: "To decide doubtful cases, Su Zhenzhi; to see the inside from the outside, Song Shigui."

literal: People of the time considered them the two marvels of the office.
idiomatic: People of the time considered them the two marvels of the office.

literal: Prisoners from the Southern Terrace who reached the Court of Justice—Shigui acquitted many and then transferred authority to the Censorate to question their abuses.
idiomatic: Prisoners from the Southern Terrace who reached the Court of Justice—Shigui acquitted many and then transferred authority to the Censorate to question their abuses.

literal: Chief Commandant Bi Yiyun did not send them; the transfer went back and forth without stop.
idiomatic: Chief Commandant Bi Yiyun did not send them; the transfer went back and forth without stop.

literal: Shigui then submitted a memorial vehemently accusing Yiyun of cruelty and usurpation.
idiomatic: Shigui then submitted a memorial vehemently accusing Yiyun of cruelty and usurpation.

literal: Emperor Wenxuan summoned the two men and personally charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long bullied the Court—you can uphold principle and resist them; only keep this heart and do not worry about lacking wealth and honor."
idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan summoned the two men and personally charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long bullied the Court—you can uphold principle and resist them; only keep this heart and do not worry about lacking wealth and honor."

literal: He charged Yiyun: "What you have done truly deserves death; because your will is set on hating evil, for now I pardon you once."
idiomatic: He charged Yiyun: "What you have done truly deserves death; because your will is set on hating evil, for now I pardon you once."

literal: He then turned to the court ministers and said: "These two are both my bone-in-the-throat ministers."
idiomatic: He then turned to the court ministers and said: "These two are both my bone-in-the-throat ministers."

literal: When he died, prisoners throughout the Court and Censorate all wept: "When Vice-Director Song dies, how can we have a way to live!"
idiomatic: When he died, prisoners throughout the Court and Censorate all wept: "When Vice-Director Song dies, how can we have a way to live!"

literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Guangzhou; his posthumous title was Ping.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Guangzhou; his posthumous title was Ping.

literal: He had no sons; Shiliang made his fifth son Chaoji heir.
idiomatic: He had no sons; Shiliang made his fifth son Chaoji heir.

literal: Fan's younger brother Shijing.
idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Shijing.

literal: From youth Shijing disciplined himself; he was known for filial service to his parents.
idiomatic: From youth Shijing disciplined himself; he was known for filial service to his parents.

literal: With his younger brother Daoyu he studied behind curtains, reading widely, especially expert in classical meaning.
idiomatic: With his younger brother Daoyu he studied behind curtains, reading widely, especially expert in classical meaning.

literal: His clansman cousin Bian greatly valued him.
idiomatic: His clansman cousin Bian greatly valued him.

literal: He was presented as a xiucai and placed in the upper grade.
idiomatic: He was presented as a xiucai and placed in the upper grade.

literal: He was twice promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Prince of Pengcheng Xie's opening office.
idiomatic: He was twice promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Prince of Pengcheng Xie's opening office.

literal: Xie loved his talent and learning and greatly esteemed him.
idiomatic: Xie loved his talent and learning and greatly esteemed him.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen greatly praised and distinguished him.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen greatly praised and distinguished him.

literal: He was promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Ministry of Education.
idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Ministry of Education.

literal: Shijing understood penal principle, compiled statutes, decided doubtful cases, and judged as if flowing water.
idiomatic: Shijing understood penal principle, compiled statutes, decided doubtful cases, and judged as if flowing water.

literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie often said: "Song Shijing is subtle and refined—talent fit for Vice-Director of the Secretariat."
idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie often said: "Song Shijing is subtle and refined—talent fit for Vice-Director of the Secretariat."

literal: For doubtful matters within the Terrace, Right Vice-Director You Zhao often entrusted them to him.
idiomatic: For doubtful matters within the Terrace, Right Vice-Director You Zhao often entrusted them to him.

literal: Shijing was talented in government and, moreover, from old diligent without slackness; he concurrently held several offices and won deep praise for achievement.
idiomatic: Shijing was talented in government and, moreover, from old diligent without slackness; he concurrently held several offices and won deep praise for achievement.

literal: Left Vice-Director Yuan Huai brought him in as Mobile Office Gentleman.
idiomatic: Left Vice-Director Yuan Huai brought him in as Mobile Office Gentleman.

literal: He inspected more than ten provinces and garrisons; dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments all won approval.
idiomatic: He inspected more than ten provinces and garrisons; dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments all won approval.

literal: He moved the seven garrisons, separately established the various posts, and clearly set watch-towers to guard against the unexpected.
idiomatic: He moved the seven garrisons, separately established the various posts, and clearly set watch-towers to guard against the unexpected.

literal: Huai greatly entrusted him; on his return he recommended him to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he was not inferior to Li Chong.
idiomatic: Huai greatly entrusted him; on his return he recommended him to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he was not inferior to Li Chong.

literal: The emperor said: "I have also heard of him."
idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have also heard of him."

literal: Later he was made General Who Subdues the Waves and Acting Governor of Xingyang; the Zheng clan of Zheng was overbearing and called hard to control.
idiomatic: Later he was made General Who Subdues the Waves and Acting Governor of Xingyang; the Zheng clan of Zheng was overbearing and called hard to control.

literal: Governor of Jizhou Zheng Shang's younger brother Yuanqing had earlier been Magistrate of Yuanling and took many bribes; the people suffered from him.
idiomatic: Governor of Jizhou Zheng Shang's younger brother Yuanqing had earlier been Magistrate of Yuanling and took many bribes; the people suffered from him.

literal: When Shijing took his post he summoned and admonished him.
idiomatic: When Shijing took his post he summoned and admonished him.

literal: Yuanqing acted as he pleased; Shijing bound him by law.
idiomatic: Yuanqing acted as he pleased; Shijing bound him by law.

literal: Yuanqing was afraid, abandoned his office, and fled.
idiomatic: Yuanqing was afraid, abandoned his office, and fled.

literal: Thereupon the subordinate counties feared his authority and none failed to reform and become solemn.
idiomatic: Thereupon the subordinate counties feared his authority and none failed to reform and become solemn.

literal: He sat all day investigating affairs and never rested.
idiomatic: He sat all day investigating affairs and never rested.

literal: Matters among the people, great or small, he always knew.
idiomatic: Matters among the people, great or small, he always knew.

literal: Exposing wrong and plucking out the hidden, he was like a spirit.
idiomatic: Exposing wrong and plucking out the hidden, he was like a spirit.

literal: Once there was a clerk whose term ended and who returned to the commandery and ate someone's chickens and pigs.
idiomatic: Once there was a clerk whose term ended and who returned to the commandery and ate someone's chickens and pigs.

literal: There was also a runner who accepted one hat from someone and also ate two chickens.
idiomatic: There was also a runner who accepted one hat from someone and also ate two chickens.

literal: Shijing shouted and told them; the clerk and runner knocked their heads and confessed guilt.
idiomatic: Shijing shouted and told them; the clerk and runner knocked their heads and confessed guilt.

literal: Thereupon above and below were awed and none dared violate the prohibition.
idiomatic: Thereupon above and below were awed and none dared violate the prohibition.

literal: He was stripped of his name because of his younger brother Daoyu's affair.
idiomatic: He was stripped of his name because of his younger brother Daoyu's affair.

literal: Shijing's fraternal affection surpassed others; when Daoyu died he wept for him with grief that moved passersby on the road.
idiomatic: Shijing's fraternal affection surpassed others; when Daoyu died he wept for him with grief that moved passersby on the road.

literal: More than a year later, in his mother's mourning, he could not bear the grief and died.
idiomatic: More than a year later, in his mother's mourning, he could not bear the grief and died.

literal: Shijing once compiled a "History of Jin" but never finished it.
idiomatic: Shijing once compiled a "History of Jin" but never finished it.

literal: His posthumous son Jiru held the post of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: His posthumous son Jiru held the post of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

literal: He once went to Qiao and Song and wrote a text mourning Ji Kang with very sound reasoning.
idiomatic: He once went to Qiao and Song and wrote a text mourning Ji Kang with very sound reasoning.

literal: Later his bedroom collapsed and crushed him to death; people mourned and pitied him.
idiomatic: Later his bedroom collapsed and crushed him to death; people mourned and pitied him.

literal: Daoyu from youth was clever and handsome; from Erudite of the Imperial Academy he was transferred to Acting Legal Clerk in Prince of Jingzhao Yu's opening office.
idiomatic: Daoyu from youth was clever and handsome; from Erudite of the Imperial Academy he was transferred to Acting Legal Clerk in Prince of Jingzhao Yu's opening office.

literal: He was punished because of Yu's rebellion.
idiomatic: He was punished because of Yu's rebellion.

literal: He composed poems and elegiac verses and sent them to friends and kin to show his wrongful suffering.
idiomatic: He composed poems and elegiac verses and sent them to friends and kin to show his wrongful suffering.

literal: Daoyu also once gave a poem to Editor Zhang Shijun; its final stanza said: "Zi bears the worry of cherishing a jade; I have the sickness of standing in the gate."
idiomatic: Daoyu also once gave a poem to Editor Zhang Shijun; its final stanza said: "Zi bears the worry of cherishing a jade; I have the sickness of standing in the gate."

literal: When Daoyu could not escape disaster, Shijun also met worldly calamity; people at the time all found it strange.
idiomatic: When Daoyu could not escape disaster, Shijun also met worldly calamity; people at the time all found it strange.

literal: Daoyu's distant nephew Xiaowang was learned and also loved compiling literary ornament.
idiomatic: Daoyu's distant nephew Xiaowang was learned and also loved compiling literary ornament.

literal: His appearance was short and ugly and he loved to judge people; opinion greatly disliked him.
idiomatic: His appearance was short and ugly and he loved to judge people; opinion greatly disliked him.

literal: He was Literary Scholar to Prince of Beiping.
idiomatic: He was Literary Scholar to Prince of Beiping.

literal: He sought entry into the Forest of Literature and failed; he therefore slandered court gentlemen and compiled twenty rolls of "Separate Records of Court Gentlemen."
idiomatic: He sought entry into the Forest of Literature and failed; he therefore slandered court gentlemen and compiled twenty rolls of "Separate Records of Court Gentlemen."

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi he changed the title to "Customs of the Eastern Pass" and broadened what he had heard and seen, compiling more than thirty rolls and presenting them.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi he changed the title to "Customs of the Eastern Pass" and broadened what he had heard and seen, compiling more than thirty rolls and presenting them.

literal: The words were mostly false and absurd, the sections redundant and messy, without the form of a composition.
idiomatic: The words were mostly false and absurd, the sections redundant and messy, without the form of a composition.

literal: At the end of the Great Elephant reign in Zhou.
idiomatic: At the end of the Great Elephant reign in Zhou.

literal: He took part in Wei Jiong's affair and was executed.
idiomatic: He took part in Wei Jiong's affair and was executed.

literal: Xu Yan, style Daomo, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang.
idiomatic: Xu Yan, whose style was Daomo, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang.

literal: His grandfather Mao served the Murong as Governor of Gaoyang.
idiomatic: His grandfather Mao served the Murong as Governor of Gaoyang.

literal: Yan from youth was orphaned and poor, loved reading, and studied the "Changes" under the monk Fawei.
idiomatic: Yan from youth was orphaned and poor, loved reading, and studied the "Changes" under the monk Fawei.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned he was ordered to perform divination; he was repeatedly verified and thus remained at the emperor's side, taking part in deliberation.
idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned he was ordered to perform divination; he was repeatedly verified and thus remained at the emperor's side, taking part in deliberation.

literal: Yan was plain, thick, and cautious; in speaking with others he did not touch inner affairs; the emperor for this treated him all the more intimately.
idiomatic: Yan was plain, thick, and cautious; in speaking with others he did not touch inner affairs; the emperor for this treated him all the more intimately.

literal: He was given the title Duke of Wuchang and made Governor of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: He was given the title Duke of Wuchang and made Governor of Xiangzhou.

literal: In the province he accepted bribes and often violated the law; edicts sternly reproved him, yet because Yan was a close minister at the emperor's heart he was not punished.
idiomatic: In the province he accepted bribes and often violated the law; edicts sternly reproved him, yet because Yan was a close minister at the emperor's heart he was not punished.

literal: He died; his posthumous title was Duke Xuan.
idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Duke Xuan.

literal: His son Xi inherited.
idiomatic: His son Xi inherited.

literal: When Xi died, his son Anren inherited.
idiomatic: When Xi died, his son Anren inherited.

literal: When Anren died, his son Yuankang inherited; the title was reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: When Anren died, his son Yuankang inherited; the title was reduced to marquis.
